column2: O Brahmin, the man who hears this best twelfth-day vow, or has it recited, gains the fruit of the Vajapeya sacrifice.
A pavilion crowded with many offerings, adorned with nets of small bells, surrounded by mirrors, chowries and pots...
In its middle he should place a "sarvatobhadra" diagram shining in five colours, and on it, O Brahmin, a pot filled with water.
Having covered the pot with a very fine, beautiful cloth, he should make an image of Lakshmi-Narayana in gold, silver or copper, O Brahmin, and place it on top.
Having bathed it with the five nectars and worshipped it in order with fragrance and the like, with sweets and cooked food as offerings, with devotion and controlled senses,
he should keep the vigil with full faith. The next morning he should worship Vishnu by the rule as before.
The image with a fee should be given to the teacher; he should feed Brahmins according to his means, without stinginess.
The wise one should give sesame as a gift, according to his ability, and make the sesame oblation properly in the fire.
A man who thus properly keeps the Lakshmi-Narayana vow enjoys great pleasures here with sons and grandsons,
is freed from all sins, and with ten thousand of his family goes to Vishnu's abode, hard to reach even for yogis.
Whether joined with a great sin or with all sins, one who offers a flag at Vishnu's house is freed from all sins.
For as many days as the flag stays on Vishnu's house, O Brahmin, so many thousands of ages he gains likeness to Hari.
The righteous who rejoice on seeing a flag raised are also freed from ten million great sins.
A flag raised on Vishnu's house, shaking its cloth, shakes off all the sins of the maker in half a moment.
He who raises a flag on Vishnu's house and constantly serves there goes to heaven by the path of the gods, as the wise king did.
One who has an unsinful mind toward sin should be known as the lowest of the low.
Yama's messengers said: "What you say is true; but these two are the worst of sinners. Sinners are to be punished by Yama; we shall take these two.
Dharma is what the Veda enjoins, and adharma is its opposite; this is the discernment of dharma and adharma. We shall take them to Yama."
Hearing this, the mighty messengers of Vishnu, angered, replied to Yama's soldiers, who thought adharma was dharma.
Vishnu's messengers said: "Alas, adharma touches even the assembly of those who see dharma; it is the great root of misfortunes for those lacking right discrimination.
Having become overseers of hell indiscriminately, why are you even now eager to commit sins?
Until their karma is exhausted even great sinners stay in dreadful hell as long as the moon, sun and stars last.
Not seeing atonement for sins previously accumulated, why shall I commit sinful deeds again and again?
The dharma enjoined by the Veda is true, true, without doubt; but we shall tell you truly the dharmas these two performed.
These two are freed from sin, devoted to serving Hari, protected by Hari; release them without delay.
She danced, and he raised a flag; at the hour of death, in Vishnu's house, by that they became sinless.
At the hour of death, even one who hears or speaks the Name once obtains the highest place; what of those devoted to service?
Whether joined with great sins or lesser sins, the man who serves Krishna, even at the end, obtains the highest goal.
Those devoted to serving ascetics and devotees of Vishnu — their messengers go quickly; even sinners reach the highest goal.
He who stays in Hari's temple for a moment or half a moment goes to the highest place; what of thirty years?
These two plastered the floor and swept it constantly; always in Hari's house they repaired the worn and broken.
These two sprinkled water and gave lamps in Hari's temple; how, O fortunate ones, do they deserve the experience of torture?"
Thus addressed, Vishnu's messengers cut their bonds at once, placed the two on the best aerial car, and went to Vishnu's supreme abode.
There, having attained nearness to the God of gods who bears the discus, O lord of sages, the two enjoyed divine pleasures for that period.
Having enjoyed divine pleasures there too, they came to this earth; here too they have incomparable wealth by grace of serving Hari.
By service to Hari done even unwillingly, O sage, they obtained such a fruit, hard to get even for the gods.
Worshipping the Lord of the universe, Madhava, willingly and with devotion, we two shall attain supreme good: that cause has been shown.
A very great fruit comes even from a deed done without will, O lord of the earth; what then of one done with faith?
Hearing this, the chief of sages Vibhandaka praised that couple and went to his penance-grove.
Therefore know, O divine sage, that serving the God of gods who bears the discus is held to be like a wish-granting cow for all.
For those devoted to Hari's worship, Hari himself, the eternal, gives the highest good, the fruit of all desires.
He who reads or hears this holy account that destroys all sins also reaches the highest goal.
Worship of Vishnu should be done thus on the full-moon day, O sage; on the eleventh and on the full-moon day a vigil should be kept.
Worship with the five nectars and so on is the same on the five days; on the full-moon day he should bathe Vishnu with milk as able; sesame oblation and sesame gift should be made.
Then, on the sixth day, having done his own rites, tasted the five cow-products, he should worship Hari by the rule.
Afterward he should feed Brahmins as his means allow, without stinginess; then with his kinsmen he should eat silently.
So, in the months from Pausha to Kartika, O Narada, the man should keep the vow in the bright fortnight by the earlier rule.
So the vow, which destroys sin, should be kept for a year; when Margashirsha comes again, the observer should perform the conclusion.
O Brahmin, on the eleventh he should fast as before; on the twelfth he should carefully taste the five cow-products.
Having properly worshipped the God of gods, Janardana, with fragrance, flowers and so on, the self-controlled one should give an offering to a Brahmin:
milk-rice mixed with honey, with ghee and fruit, fragrant water, a full pot, and a fee,
the pot covered with cloth with five gems; he should give it to a Brahmin who knows the Self, O lord of sages.
O Self of all, lord of all beings, all-pervading, eternal — be pleased, Madhava, with this gift of the best food.
Having given the milk-rice with this, he should feed Brahmins as able, and then eat himself silently with kinsmen.
He who keeps this vow, called the "five of Hari", never returns from Brahma's world.
This vow should be kept by those wishing the supreme liberation, O Brahmin; it is like a forest fire to the wilderness of all sins.
The fruit one would get by giving ten million thousand cows is obtained by men through fasting for this.
He who hears this with devotion, devoted to Narayana, is freed from the most dreadful ten million torments.

I was fasting there, and with a few people kept a vigil at night, without an army.
naradapuran:22:65	Wearied by the journey and afflicted by hunger and thirst, at the end of the vigil there I died, father.
naradapuran:22:66	Then, bound by Yama's soldiers, terrifying with huge tusks, I was brought by a road full of many torments to Yama; I saw the Judge with fangs and a fearful face.
naradapuran:22:67	Then Yama called Chitragupta and said: 'Tell the proper punishment for this man, O wise one.'
naradapuran:22:68	Thus addressed by the king of dharma, Chitragupta, the best, reflected long and again said:
naradapuran:22:69	'This one was given to sin, true; yet hear, protector of dharma: one who fasts on the eleventh is freed from all sins.
naradapuran:22:70	On the day of Hari, on the lovely bank of the Reva, he fasted without food, kept the vigil, and became free of sin.
naradapuran:22:71	Whatever sins he has done, and they are very many, all are destroyed by the power of the fast.'
naradapuran:22:72	Thus told by the wise Chitragupta, the king of dharma, moved by compassion, prostrated himself on the ground before me,
naradapuran:22:73	and the lord of dharma honoured me with devotion there. Then he called all his soldiers and said:
naradapuran:22:74	Yama said: 'Hear my words, messengers; I shall tell you the highest good. Honour men devoted to the path of dharma and bring them near me.
naradapuran:22:75	Those who delight in worshipping Vishnu, who are pure, grateful, devoted to the eleventh-day vow, masters of senses, who peacefully say always Narayana, Achyuta, Hari, be my refuge" — leave them quickly.

Those who always say "Narayana, Achyuta, Janardana, Krishna, Vishnu, Lord of Lakshmi, Padmanabha, Shiva, Shankara," peaceful, for the good of all the world — O soldiers, leave them from afar; my discipline is not for them.

Those who offer their deeds to Narayana, devoted to Hari, intent on the path of right conduct, servants of teachers, devoted to giving to the worthy and to protecting the poor — O messengers, always leave those attached to Hari's name.

Those free of association with heretics, firm in devotion to Brahmins, eager for the company of the good, hospitable, who see Shiva and Hari with equal regard, and devoted to helping others — O messengers, leave them.

Those devoid of the nectar of Hari's stories and whose minds are not intent on remembering Narayana, who are not gladdened by sprinkling water on the feet of Brahmins — bring those sinners to my house.

Those who revile their mother and father, who hate the world and do harm to the well-wishing, who are fond of stealing the property of the gods, destroyers of people, devoted to wrongdoing — O messengers, bring them here.
